                                     IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

                              R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE
                                            FIR/ORDER) NO. 18659 of 2023


                       FOR APPROVAL AND SIGNATURE:


                       HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE P. M. RAVAL
                       ==========================================================

                                    Approved for Reporting                    Yes           No

                       ==========================================================
                                             JATIN NARENDRABHAI SANGHVI & ORS.
                                                            Versus
                                                   STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
                       ==========================================================
                       Appearance:
                       MR EKANT G AHUJA(5323) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3
                       NOTICE SERVED for the Respondent(s) No. 2
                       MR ROHAN SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
                       ==========================================================

                         CORAM:HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE P. M. RAVAL

                                                          Date : 19/06/2026

                                                            JUDGMENT

1.        Rule fixed forthwith. Learned APP waives service of rule
                       on behalf of the respondent - State.

2.        The petitioners have approached this Court by invoking
                       its inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of
                       Criminal Procedure, 1973, seeking quashing and setting aside
                       of FIR being C.R. No. 11191034230027/2023 registered with
                       Naranpura Police Station, Ahmedabad, and the consequent
                       Sessions Case No. 61 of 2023 pending before the learned
                       Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ahmedabad (Rural) at



                                                              Page 1 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                             Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                          NEUTRAL CITATION




                            R/CR.MA/18659/2023                           JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                         undefined




                       Mirzapur, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420
                       and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, Sections 66-C and 66-D of
                       the Information Technology Act, 2000, Section 23(I) (A), (F), (G)
                       and (H) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, and
                       Sections 4 and 5 of the Gambling Act.

3.        The facts of the prosecution in nutshell is to the effect
                       the complainant that on 21.02.2023, in Shop/Office No.103,
                       Omshri Gokul Complex, Near Naranpura Stadium road, one
                       person was found (Jatin Narendrabhai Sanghvi), and one not
                       arrested person from this person Rs.50,000/- were found, and
                       also an Exchange Betting Application THE TIGER 247 was
                       found and the same was operated with one forged ID named
                       JATIN9898. That on that particular day there was a match
                       between Nepal and Scotland and an online bet of Rs. 4145/-
                       was made on winning losing of the team, the said person had
                       gambled and unauthorizedly made calls to the not caught
                       person (2) Vipul Badshah, residing in Navrangpur (3) Vikubhai
                       Tinabhai had subsequently made entry in diary by using
                       mobile phone. Further, although the said person is not a
                       recognized member or agent of any Stock Exchange authorized
                       by the SEBI/Government of India then also for their own
                       financial gain illegally and unauthorizedly carried out trading
                       of Share Market deals funds in winning-losing. During the
                       raid while searching the person one mobile phone was found
                       of Value Rs. 10,000/- and cash of Rs. 20,000/-, further diary
                       of Value of Rs.00/- and light bill of value of Rs. 00/- was
                       found thus total muddamal of value Rs. 30,000/- was found


                                                          Page 2 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                      Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                          NEUTRAL CITATION




                            R/CR.MA/18659/2023                           JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                         undefined




                       and were taken into custody as per the details of panchnama.
                       That FIR is filed for the offences punishable under Sections
                       406, 420, 114 of the IPC, under Sections 66 (C)-(D) of the IT
                       Act, under Sections 4 and 5 of the Gambling Act and Under
                       Sections 23 (e), 23 (A), (F), (G), (H) of the Security Contract
                       Regulation Act, 1956.

4.        Learned advocate for the petitioners submitted that the
                       petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present offence
                       and have no connection whatsoever with the allegations
                       levelled in the FIR.

4.1 It was further submitted that, in view of the bar contained
                       under Section 26 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act,
                       1956, the Sessions Court could not have taken cognizance on
                       the basis of a police report (charge-sheet) in the absence of a
                       written complaint before the competent Court. Therefore, the
                       proceedings, to the extent they pertain to the offences under
                       the said Act, are without jurisdiction and liable to be quashed.

4.2 It was also submitted that a bare reading of the FIR does
                       not disclose the ingredients of the offences punishable under
                       Sections 406, 420 and 114 of the IPC or Sections 66C and
                       66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000. Accordingly, it
                       was urged that the present petition deserves to be allowed.

5.        Per contra, learned APP opposed the petition and


                                                          Page 3 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                      Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                                   NEUTRAL CITATION




                            R/CR.MA/18659/2023                                    JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                                  undefined




                       submitted that during the raid, petitioner No.1 was found
                       present at the place of occurrence. It was submitted that
                       various incriminating articles, including documents, a diary
                       and mobile phones, were recovered from the spot. According to
                       the prosecution, the material collected during the course of
                       investigation prima facie reveals the involvement of the
                       present petitioners in the alleged offences, particularly the
                       offences of criminal breach of trust as well as the offences
                       under         the         Securities   Contracts       (Regulation)        Act,       the
                       Information Technology Act and the Gambling Act. It was,
                       therefore, urged that the present petition, being devoid of
                       merits, deserves to be dismissed.

6.        Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.

7.        It transpires from the FIR that on 21.02.2023, while the
                       complainant and other police officials were on patrolling duty,
                       they received secret information that certain persons were
                       engaged in "dubba trading" without authorization from SEBI
                       or any recognized stock exchange and were thereby indulging
                       in illegal trading activities. Acting upon the said information, a
                       raid was conducted at the place in question, where the
                       petitioners were allegedly found engaged in online buying and
                       selling of shares through mobile trading applications.

8.        However, upon perusal of the FIR and the charge-sheet
                       papers, this Court finds no material to suggest entrustment of


                                                               Page 4 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                               Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                                 NEUTRAL CITATION




                            R/CR.MA/18659/2023                                  JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                                undefined




                       any property to the petitioners, which is an essential
                       ingredient of the offence under Section 406 of the IPC. There is
                       no statement or document on record indicating that any
                       property was entrusted to the petitioners and that they
                       dishonestly misappropriated the same.

9.        Likewise, no material has been placed on record to show
                       that any person suffered financial loss or that the petitioners
                       obtained any wrongful gain. The investigating agency has also
                       failed to produce any concrete evidence in support of the
                       allegation of cheating. In the absence of any material showing
                       criminal breach of trust or dishonest inducement leading to
                       delivery of property, the ingredients of Sections 406 and 420 of
                       the IPC are not made out against the petitioners.

10.       A bare reading of the aforesaid provision makes it clear
                       that no Court can take cognizance of an offence punishable
                       under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 except
                       upon a complaint made by the Central Government, the State
                       Government, SEBI, a recognized stock exchange, or any
                       person duly authorized in this behalf. Even assuming that the
                       complainant               was      an   authorized     person,      the       statute
                       contemplates a complaint before the competent Court and not
                       registration of an FIR. Therefore, prima facie, no case under
                       Section 23 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956
                       is made out.

NEUTRAL CITATION




                           R/CR.MA/18659/2023                            JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                         undefined

11.      So far as Sections 66C and 66D of the Information
                       Technology Act, 2000 are concerned, Section 66C relates to
                       identity theft, whereas Section 66D deals with cheating by
                       personation through the use of a computer resource. Upon
                       perusal of the FIR and the charge-sheet papers, no material is
                       found to suggest that the petitioners forged or dishonestly
                       used the electronic identity of any other person. There is also
                       no material to show that the petitioners created any fake
                       profile, gained unauthorized access to any account, or cheated
                       any person by impersonation through a computer resource.

12.      Not an iota of oral or documentary evidence has been
                       placed on record to demonstrate how the petitioners cheated
                       any person or impersonated another individual for the
                       purpose of cheating. Mere use of a mobile phone, in the
                       absence of such material, would not attract the provisions of
                       Sections 66C or 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

13.      Further, as observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
                       Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh,
                       reported in (2024) INSC 626 the offences under Sections 406
                       and 420 of the IPC operate in distinct fields. In the facts of the
                       present case, the ingredients of Section 420 of the IPC are also
                       required to be independently established.

14.        So far as offence under Section 420 of the IPC is
                       concerned, it is appropriate to refer to the decision of the


                                                          Page 6 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                      Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                          NEUTRAL CITATION




                           R/CR.MA/18659/2023                            JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                         undefined




                       Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rekha Jain vs. The State of
                       Karnataka & Anr. reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 468, wherein
                       the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that, to make out a case
                       against a person for the offence under Section 420 of IPC,
                       there must be a dishonest inducement to deceive a person to
                       deliver any property to any other person. Further, in the case
                       of Sarabjit Kaur vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported in
                       (2023) 5 SCC 360 has held in paragraph No.13 as follows:

"13. A breach of contract does not give rise to criminal
                               prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or
                               dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of
                               the transaction. Merely on the allegation of failure to
                               keep up promise will not be enough to initiate criminal
                               proceedings. From the facts available on record, it is
                               evident that the respondent No.2 had improved his
                               case ever since the first complaint was filed in which
                               there were no allegations against the appellant rather
                               it was only against the property dealers which was in
                               subsequent complaints that the name of the appellant
                               was mentioned. On the first complaint, the only
                               request was for return of the amount paid by the
                               respondent No.2. When the offence was made out on
                               the basis of the first complaint, the second complaint
                               was filed with improved version making allegations
                               against the appellant as well which was not there in
                               the earlier complaint. The entire idea seems to be to
                               convert a civil dispute into criminal and put pressure
                               on the appellant for return of the amount allegedly
                               paid. The criminal Courts are not meant to be used for
                               settling scores or pressurise parties to settle civil
                               disputes. Wherever ingredients of criminal offences are
                               made out, criminal courts have to take cognizance. The


                                                          Page 7 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                      Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                          NEUTRAL CITATION




                           R/CR.MA/18659/2023                            JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                         undefined




                               complaint in question on the basis of which F.I.R. was
                               registered was filed nearly three years after the last
                               date fixed for registration of the sale deed. Allowing
                               the proceedings to continue would be an abuse of
                               process of the Court."

15.1 Tested on the anvil of the aforesaid principles, the
                       offence punishable under Section 420 of the IPC is not
                       made out, for the reasons recorded hereinabove.

16.      In the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, reported
                       in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, the Apex Court has set out the
                       categories of cases in which the inherent power under Section
                       482 CrPC can be exercised and held in para 102 as under:

"102. In the backdrop of the interpretation of the
                                various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter
                                XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this
                                Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise
                                of the extraordinary power under Art. 226 or the
                                inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which
                                we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the
                                following categories of cases by way of illustration
                                wherein such power could be exercised either to
                                prevent abuse of the process of any court or
                                otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may
                                not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly
                                defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible
                                guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive
                                list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power



                                                          Page 8 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                      Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                                   NEUTRAL CITATION




                           R/CR.MA/18659/2023                                     JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                                  undefined




                                should be exercised:

(1) Where the allegations made in the first information
                                report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their
                                face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima
                                facie constitute any offence or make out a case
                                against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the first information
                                report and other materials, if any, accompanying the
                                FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an
                                investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of
                                the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within
                                the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the
                                FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support
                                of the same do not disclose the commission of any
                                offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute
                                a     cognizable          offence     but     constitute      only       a
                                noncognizable offence, no investigation is permitted
                                by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as
                                contemplated under sec. 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or
                                complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable
                                on the basis of which no prudent person can ever

                                                               Page 9 of 12
Uploaded by MOHD SAIF ULLAH(HC02372) on Fri Jun 19 2026                               Downloaded on : Sat Jun 20 02:05:28 IST 2026
                                                                                                                        NEUTRAL CITATION




                           R/CR.MA/18659/2023                                          JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                                       undefined




                                reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground
                                for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in
                                any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act
                                (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to
                                the institution and continuance of the proceedings
                                and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code
                                or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for
                                the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(7)    Where         a    criminal     proceeding        is    manifestly
                                attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding
                                is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for
                                wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view
                                to spite him due to private and personal grudge."

16.1 Tested on the anvil of the principles laid down in the
                       aforesaid          judgments,            particularly        sub-para         (6)     of
                       paragraph 102, and having found that there exists a legal
                       bar      under        Section       26     of   the       Securities     Contracts
                       (Regulation) Act, 1956, no offence under the said Act can
                       be said to be made out. Further, applying the principles
                       laid down in sub-para (3) of paragraph 102 of Bhajan Lal
                       (supra), even if the allegations contained in the FIR and
                       the material collected during investigation are accepted at
                       their face value, they do not disclose the commission of
                       any offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the
                       IPC or Sections 66C and 66D of the Information
                       Technology Act, 2000.

NEUTRAL CITATION




                           R/CR.MA/18659/2023                                           JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                                                                                                                        undefined

17.      Resultantly, the present application succeeds and is
                       partly          allowed.           The      FIR          being        C.R.           No.
                       11191034230027/2023 registered with Naranpura Police
                       Station, Ahmedabad, and the consequent Sessions Case
                       No. 61 of 2023 pending before the learned Principal
                       District and Sessions Judge, Ahmedabad (Rural) at
                       Mirzapur, for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
                       420 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, Sections 66C and
                       66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Section
                       23(I), (A), (F), (G) and (H) of the Securities Contracts
                       (Regulation) Act, 1956, and Sections 4 and 5 of the
                       Gambling Act, together with all consequential proceedings
                       arising therefrom, are hereby quashed and set aside qua
                       the present petitioners.

18.      Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent. Direct
                       service is permitted.

19.      Insofar         as   the   remaining            offences     are      concerned,
                       including those under the Gujarat Prevention of Gambling Act,
                       1887, the Investigating Agency and the concerned Court shall
                       be at liberty to proceed further in accordance with law.

20.      It is clarified that if any additional material surfaces
                       during the course of further investigation or upon receipt of
                       the FSL report, the same may be considered by the
                       Investigating Agency and the competent Court in accordance


                                                                Page 11 of 12

                                                                                                           NEUTRAL CITATION




                           R/CR.MA/18659/2023                             JUDGMENT DATED: 19/06/2026

                       with law. However, such material shall not revive or affect the
                       offences which have been quashed by this Court.

(P. M. RAVAL, J)

notes: Fetched via indiankanoon_client.get_document() (live API), cleaned via ik_text_cleaner.clean_document(). Phase 3c of the loc-transit-remand-plan, 2026-09-05: a Section 482 CrPC quashing petition where the FIR alleged, among other charges (IPC 406/420/114, securities law, gambling law), Sections 66C (identity theft) and 66D (cheating by personation) of the IT Act. The Court quashed those counts for lack of material -- no evidence the petitioners forged/misused another's electronic identity, created a fake profile, gained unauthorized access, or cheated by impersonation via a computer resource. Directly useful, real-shaped precedent for the recurring 'bare invocation of 66C/66D isn't enough' pattern -- same family of holding as Usha Chakraborty's bare-Section-323 finding from an earlier batch. See chunks/jatin_narendrabhai_sanghvi_v_state_of_gujarat_chunks.json (chunk_method='curated_excerpt') for the curated holding.
